title: Redwood Security BCDR / Incident Response / SLA Escalation Review - Polaris Financial
summary: Redwood and Polaris reviewed incident response, BCDR objectives (RTO/RPO), SLA uptime targets and escalation paths. Polaris asked about multi-region failover, audit logs, KMS encryption, SSO/RBAC, and Redwood's post-incident processes. Agreed next steps: share SOC 2 package, SLA and escalation matrix, runbook export, schedule a tabletop DR exercise and provide a dedicated pilot environment for a failover test.
next_steps: John to send SOC 2 + ISO package link and SLA doc (by 2025-11-22)
Priya to share runbook export and escalation matrix (by 2025-11-24)
Schedule DR tabletop with Polaris stakeholders (target week of 2025-12-08)
Set up dedicated pilot workspace for failover test (Daniel to coordinate)
Kyle to provide Polaris' RTO/RPO targets and compliance checklist (by 2025-11-25)

Priya Shah | Export and share Redwood runbook and escalation matrix (PDF) | 2025-11-24
Daniel Cho | Provision dedicated pilot env and invite Polaris SREs | 2025-11-28

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-20 15:00 UTC, Duration: ~42 minutes. Attendees: John (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Martin (CTO, Polaris), Laura (Head of Security, Polaris), Kyle (SRE), Anita (Compliance).

[00:00] John: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is John from Redwood, with Priya and Daniel. How's it goin?
[00:08] Martin: Morning, John. Thanks, we scheduled this to go through incident response, BCDR, RTO/RPO and escalation. Laura and I will lead questions.
[00:14] Laura: Yes, we have a list. We want to understand your SLA, how you do failover and who we call when things go bump in the night.
[00:22] John: Totally, that's the plan. Priya do you want to start with a quick overview of the incident response model?
[00:27] Priya: Sure. So, Redwood's IR process is tiered — detection, Triage, escalation, mitigation, post-mortem. We use an internal pager system for severity 1s, and we have an engineering on-call rotation. Sev1 is outage impacting production inference for >5 minutes or major data loss. For Sev1 we aim for a 15 minute acknowledgement window and we have runbooks tied to model variants and deployment types — hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[01:02] Kyle: Can you clarify the RTO and RPO commitments? Our legal team will want numbers to put into contracts.
[01:08] Priya: For hosted customers, our standard SLA guarantees 99.9% uptime for API endpoints (monthly) with contractual RTOs for dedicated contracts; we typically target RTO of 1 hour for critical path failures in dedicated pools and RPO depends on caching and persistence — default RPO is near-zero for metadata, token streams are ephemeral. For stateful KV cache, our recommended pattern is asynchronous replication to reduce RPO to under 5 minutes in multi-region configs.
[01:42] Martin: "Near-zero for metadata" — can you be more specific? We can't have ambiguity there.
[01:46] Priya: Sure, metadata like model configs, version pins, rollout policies are persisted to our control plane with strong consistency; changes are journaled and replicated across control plane nodes. For dedicated/private, customers can choose to bring their own DB or use our replicated store — that affects RPO. For legal we can put explicit RPO numbers in the SOW for Dedicated.
[02:10] Laura: On encryption — do you support BYOK and KMS integrations? We need to know who controls keys.
[02:16] Daniel: Yes. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. For Dedicated we offer KMS integration with customer-managed keys where feasible; for Hosted we use platform-managed envelope encryption by default, and we can support customer keys under enterprise contracts. All at-rest data is AES-256 and in transit is TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3).
[02:44] Anita: What about audit logs and retention? We have to keep logs for 7 years for certain transactions.
[02:49] Priya: We capture admin audit logs (who changed rollout policies, who accessed models), API access logs, and operational logs. Retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we have tiers — default 90 days, can extend for a fee or via enterprise contract. We can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[03:15] Kyle: Regarding RPO for KV cache — you mentioned async replication — if RegionA goes down how long to failover and is there data loss window?
[03:22] Priya: Failover depends on policy: automatic regional failover is supported for Dedicated with active/passive. RPO is typically the replication lag, we target under 5 minutes but dependent on traffic and sequence lengths for cache. For strict RPO you should enable synchronous replication or use Private deployment with your own persistence.
[03:46] Martin: SLA credits — what's the formula if you miss 99.9?
[03:50] John: Our SLA doc defines credit tiers. For instance, <99.9% but >=99.0% gets X% credits, below 99.0% more. We will send the official SLA PDF; baseline hosted is 99.9. Dedicated SLAs are negotiable with higher SLOs for committed capacity.
[04:05] Laura: Escalation — who do we call? Are there phone numbers, and can we get an on-call email and phone?
[04:12] Daniel: Yes, we have a 24/7 on-call rotation for Sev1 for Dedicated customers. We provide an escalation matrix in the security portal: front-line support (support@redwood or ticket), then AE/CSM, then SE on-call, then engineering pager. For Enterprise we include an escalation phone tree and named contacts.
[04:35] Kyle: How fast do you escalate internally?
[04:37] Priya: For Sev1 we escalate immediately on detection; on-call acknowledges within 15 minutes and engineering starts mitigation. There's an SLA for acknowledgement and a separate track for remediation windows.
[04:49] Martin: Can we get an example of a past incident postmortem format? We need to see how thorough your RCAs are.
[04:55] John: We'll share redacted PMs, yes. We do blameless postmortems, timeline, mitigating steps, root cause, follow-ups, and permanent fixes.
[05:05] Laura: Do you do quarterly disaster recovery tests?
[05:07] Priya: We encourage quarterly tabletop exercises with customers for Dedicated/Private. Redwood runs internal chaos tests and can coordinate a joint failover test in a dedicated pilot environment.
[05:22] Anita: Data residency — our customers require EU-only processing and logs within EU. How do you support region locking?
[05:29] Daniel: We provide regional tenancy and data residency controls. For Hosted we can provision regional clusters and restrict backups/log exports to the region. For Private you control everything. For Dedicated we can configure region-specific capacity and ensure backups remain in-region.
[05:47] Martin: Ok good. Now about notifications and P1 incident cadence — do you provide bridge calls and status page updates?
[05:54] Priya: Yes, we will create a dedicated incident bridge and update status.redwood.ai publicly for hosted and a private status feed for Dedicated customers. We also do push notifications via the support portal and email to the escalation list.
[06:08] Kyle: For the bridge, who runs it? Is it Redwood or shared?
[06:11] Daniel: Redwood will run the primary bridge for hosted incidents. For joint exercises or Dedicated we can set up a shared bridge and include your SRE.
[06:21] Martin: I want specifics on the escalation matrix. Can you walk through it?
[06:24] Priya: Sure. Step 1: monitoring alerts create ticket at severity level. Step 2: support Tier 1 triages; if it's Sev2+ they notify SE. Sev1 triggers immediate pager to SE on-call and CSM/AE. Step 3: if unresolved after 30 minutes, engineering lead paged; after 60 min exec notified. All steps recorded in timeline. We will send you a PDF with thresholds and phone numbers.
[06:50] Laura: Are your incident timelines auditable? We need proof for auditors.
[06:54] John: Yes, we keep immutable logs for incident timelines and chat transcripts. For Dedicated/Private we can provide access to those logs under NDA.
[07:06] Anita: Compliance — you mentioned SOC2 and ISO earlier. Can we see evidence?
[07:10] John: Absolutely. We'll share the latest SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate through our secure portal. We'll also include the scope that maps to data processing for inference.
[07:21] Laura: On RBAC and SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Support for fine-grained roles is a must.
[07:29] Daniel: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We have RBAC that can scope to project, model, and environment levels. For privileged actions (e.g., rollback, export) we log approvals and require MFA for privileged accounts.
[07:47] Kyle: How are audit logs correlated with user identities? If someone invokes the API with a service account, can we map back to a user action?
[07:53] Priya: Yes, we include identity mapping in logs. Service token usage is logged and linked to its owner in the provisioning system; we can provide UIDs and timestamps.
[08:05] Martin: Any limits around log exports — size or frequency?
[08:09] Daniel: We stream to S3 or push to your SIEM via event forwarding in near real time. For massive volumes we batch and compress; there's a cost tier for very high retention.
[08:22] Laura: For encryption key ownership — if we use BYOK and there's a subpoena, do you have a process to handle lawful requests?
[08:30] John: We have legal and compliance workflows. If keys are customer-managed and stored customer-side, Redwood cannot decrypt without your consent. For hosted keys we follow legal process and notify customers as appropriate per contract. We can detail the lawful access process in the artefacts we send.
[08:50] Kyle: Let's talk about realistic failover: say region A has a complete outage — what's the sequence and estimated time to route traffic to region B for dedicated?
[08:58] Priya: For Dedicated with active/passive multi-region: automatically detect via our health checks, promote passive to active, sync KV cache if available — typical cutover for stateless requests can be sub-5 minutes; for stateful workloads it's dependent on replication. If you want guaranteed sub-5 minute RTO for certain models, best to have pre-warmed instances in the failover region.
[09:26] Martin: Do you provide runbooks we can ingest into our incident management system?
[09:30] Daniel: Yes, runbooks are exportable in markdown/JSON and can be integrated. We'll attach a sample runbook and the full set for your environment.
[09:39] Anita: Regarding post-incident communication — do you provide a summary template and timing?
[09:43] Priya: After every Sev1 we publish an initial inside-24h update, then a full RCA within 72 hours and a final permanence plan within two weeks. We also capture mitigations and owners.
[09:54] Kyle: On testing — we'll want to run a tabletop and then a staged failover in a pilot. What are risks to the production models?
[10:00] John: Doing a staged failover in a dedicated pilot environment avoids production risk. For hosted customers we can coordinate a read-only test or use canary routing to mirror traffic. We'll help design the experiment.
[10:16] Martin: Security team will want to review the escalation matrix and the names of engineers who will be on-call for our account. Is that ok?
[10:24] John: Yes, we can provide named contacts under NDA and include escalation phone numbers.
[10:28] Laura: A few quick nitty-gritty: 1) audit log immutability — WORM storage? 2) log signing? 3) tamper-evidence?
[10:36] Priya: We support WORM-style retention for S3 exports and can provide signed digests for logs for tamper evidence. For Hosted we can provide the signed manifests upon request.
[10:47] Anita: How do you assure uptime during rolling upgrades?
[10:50] Daniel: We do canary rollouts and traffic shifting; models are versioned and canaryed across a percentage of traffic. We have automatic fallback when latency or error rates spike. For Dedicated we run upgrade windows and can schedule in coordination with your team.
[11:06] Kyle: On observability — can we see token-level latency and cost breakdown for our routes?
[11:11] John: Yes, in Redwood Console you can drill down per-route, per-model, see p50/p95/p99 latencies and token costs; those dashboards are part of the offering and can be shared read-only with your SREs.
[11:25] Martin: Let's talk about a hypothetical incident timeline example — can you outline roles and times?
[11:30] Priya: (walks through example) t0 monitoring alert, t+2m ticket created, t+5m Tier 1 triage, t+10m SE paged, t+15m SE acknowledges and opens bridge, t+30-60m mitigation in place, t+4h permanent patch scheduled. All captured in timeline.
[12:00] Laura: If we require audit logs to be immutable and retained for 7 years, what would be the estimated cost?
[12:05] Daniel: It'll depend on volume. We'll provide an estimate after we get your average event rate; generally long-term cold storage costs apply and we can export to your cloud storage to reduce cost.
[12:20] Martin: On the legal side — if we include these specifics in our SOW, do you accept contractual SLA playoffs?
[12:25] John: Yes, for Dedicated we negotiate SLAs and uptime targets in the SOW and there are remedies/credits defined. We'll work with legal.
[12:34] Kyle: Any restrictions on running chaos engineering tools against your dedicated pool?
[12:38] Priya: We allow controlled chaos tests in dedicated and private if pre-coordinated. We require a test plan and schedule to avoid surprises.
[12:48] Anita: For audit readiness, can we run joint audits or on-site inspections for Private deployments?
[12:53] Daniel: For Private yes; for Dedicated we offer virtual audits and can provide artifacts. On-site visits depend on contractual terms.
[13:05] Martin: Alright, recap?
[13:08] John: Recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO, the SLA PDF, escalation matrix and sample postmortem. Priya will share runbook exports and we will provision a dedicated pilot for a staged failover test. Polaris to share RTO/RPO targets and retention specs. Schedule tabletop for early December.
[13:30] Laura: Sounds good, thanks.
[13:33] Martin: Thanks all.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions ("red wood" vs Redwood), and some technical terms abbreviated inconsistently (KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cache). End of call.
